Name: Automate UI - MachineAutomation

Description:
[b][size=5]Warehouse Automation[/size]
[/b]
[b]Warehouse Automation[/b] helps you automate your Stardew Valley farm. By linking chests to your machines through simple, logical names, you can automatically load raw ingredients into your machines and harvest the finished products back into your chests.
The best part? [b]Your chests and machines do not need to be next to each other.[/b] They can be placed anywhere on your farm, inside sheds, greenhouses, barns, or cellars, and the mod will link them instantly across map boundaries.

[b]Rule Editor Input Text Syntax Guide[/b]

The mod uses a flexible text parser to determine what ingredients are required,
how many of them are needed, and what crop qualities are allowed.

1. [u]The "Collect-Only" Rule (No Inputs)[/u]

Use this when you want your machines to run passively on their own. The mod will
only harvest the machine when it is ready and will never try to put items inside
it.

  - Keywords: Empty, None, or Blank (case-insensitive)
  - What it means: The mod checks the machine, gathers its output, and restarts
    it (if it supports standard passive looping like Worm Bins or Mushroom
    Logs).
  - Example: Empty

2. [u]Standard Single Item Rule[/u]

The most common syntax for standard processing.

  - Syntax: [Item Name]-[Count]
  - What it means: The machine requires exactly the specified count of the item.
    It accepts any quality (no star, silver, gold, or iridium).
  - Examples:
      - Egg-1 (Loads 1 Egg of any quality)
      - Copper Ore-5 (Loads 5 Copper Ore of any quality)

3.[u] Single Item with Quality Filters[/u]

Use this to restrict which star qualities are allowed to be fed into your
machines.

  - Syntax: [Item Name]-[Quality]-[Count]
  - Quality Keywords:
      - Normal (No Star): normal, regular, or 0
      - Silver Star: silver or 1
      - Gold Star: gold or 2
      - Iridium Star (Purple): iridium or 4
  - Using Multiple Allowed Qualities: You can list multiple qualities separated
    by a backslash (\) or forward slash (/).
  - Examples:
      - Melon-normal-1 (Only loads standard Melons with no star)
      - Cheese-normal\silver\gold-1 (Allows normal, silver, or gold cheese, but
        protects premium Iridium Cheese from being put in a machine)
      - Pumpkin-0/1-1 (Only loads normal [0] or silver [1] pumpkins)

4. [u]Multi-Item Rules (Complex Recipes)[/u]

Use this for machines that require more than one type of ingredient to start
processing.

  - Syntax: [First Item]-[Count];[Second Item]-[Count]
  - Rules:
      - Separate each ingredient with a semicolon (;).
      - You can mix and match standard items and quality filters in the same
        line.
  - Examples:
      - Copper Ore-5;Coal-1 (Requires 5 Copper Ore and 1 Coal)
      - Large Milk-normal\silver-1;Sugar-5 (Requires 1 normal or silver Large
        Milk, and 5 Sugar)

5. [u]Items with Hyphens in Their Name[/u]

The parser is designed to be smart. If an item name naturally contains a hyphen,
the code will automatically detect that the hyphen is part of the name and not a
separator, provided your quality filters use the correct keywords listed above.

  - Examples:
      - Pre-historic Skull-5 (The parser successfully reads the name as
        Pre-historic Skull and the count as 5)
      - Strange-looking Doll-normal-1 (The parser successfully reads the name as
        Strange-looking Doll, the allowed quality as normal, and the count as 1)

Summary Cheat Sheet

| Input Text                        |  What Machine Requires            | Allowed Qualities                  |
| :----------------------            | :--------------------                           | :----------------------------           |
| `Empty`                           | None (Collect only)                     | N/A                                        |
| `Wheat-1`                        | 1 Wheat                                      | Normal, Silver, Gold, Iridium |

| `Salmon-gold\iridium-1`  | 1 Salmon                                     | Gold or Iridium quality only   |

[b]Advanced Features: Grouping and Reserves[/b]

As your farm grows, you will naturally add more machines and chest networks. To
prevent your lists from becoming cluttered and to protect your vital crafting
materials, this mod includes two built-in organization tools: Grouping and
Reserves.

1. [u]Rule Grouping[/u]

Grouping allows you to folder and organize your automation rules directly inside
the Warehouse list view.

How it works:

  - Creation: In the Rule Editor, you can type any name in the Group field (or
    select an existing one from your dropdown list). If left blank, it defaults
    to "Default".
  - Collapsing & Expanding: In your main Warehouse list (U), rules are sorted
    under their group names. You can click on any Group Header to collapse or
    expand it.
      - A + symbol next to the group name means it is collapsed.
      - A - symbol means it is expanded.
  - Organizing: This makes it incredibly easy to clean up your UI. For example,
    you can collapse your entire "Brewing" group of rules while you are actively
    editing or reviewing your "Smelting" group of rules.

Example Groups:

  - Smelting (Furnaces, Charcoal Kilns)
  - Artisan (Kegs, Preserves Jars, Cheese Presses, Mayonnaise Machines)
  - Fishing (Crab Pots, Worm Bins)
  - Seed Making (Seed Makers)

2. [u]Item Reserves[/u]

The Reserve system acts as a safety lock. It allows you to tell the automation
network: "Never let my machines touch these items unless I have more than this
specific amount."

Why you need it:

If you automate a Furnace to turn Copper Ore and Coal into copper bars, your
system will automatically consume all of your Coal. This means you won't have
any Coal left over to craft torches, seed makers, or preserve jars.

By setting a Reserve Limit, you protect your personal crafting stocks.

How it works:

1.  Open your Warehouse Menu (U) and click the Reserves button.
2.  Select any item (like Coal) from your connected inventory grid.
3.  In the Reserve Count box, type your limit (for example, 50).
4.  Click Set.

What happens in the background:

The mod calculates your available items using the formula:
\text{Available Items} = \text{Total Items in Chests} - \text{Reserve Limit}

If your total Coal drops to 50 or below, your furnaces will immediately pause
smelting and wait, showing the status: Need Coal (50 reserved) in your rules
list. The furnaces will only start smelting again once you deposit more than 50
Coal into your chests.

Useful Reserve Recommendations:

  - Coal: Set to 50 (Protects coal for standard crafting).
  - Wood / Hardwood: Set to 100 (Protects wood for building upgrades and
    crafting fences/kegs).
  - Gold / Iridium Ore: Set to 20 (Protects ore for crafting mega bombs or
    upgrading tools).
  - Bait: Set to 100 (Ensures you always have bait left over for your personal
    fishing rod).
